page: Amazon Web Services t2.medium is an entry-tier, burstable virtual instance operating within the Xen hypervisor environment. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz on the i386 CPU architecture, delivering two physical cores and two vCPUs without symmetric multithreading enabled. The instance provides 4.0 GB of system memory, matching a resource ratio of 2.0 GB per core, supported by a 45 MB shared L3 cache and AVX instruction sets. There is no bundled local storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, and baseline network throughput is rated at 0 Gbps.

Benchmark results place the instance consistently in the bottom quartiles across computational tests. Geekbench evaluates the dual-core configuration at 852.0 for single-core execution and 1519.0 for multi-core throughput, while the PassMark CPU suite rates overall computational capability at 2834.28. Synthetic stress testing through stress-ng scores 681.79 on both single-core and multi-core evaluations. Memory access speeds demonstrate substantial tiering, recording 153.48 GB/sec in small cached reads but tapering to 17.58 GB/sec for large uncached block reads and 12.64 GB/sec for block writes.

Given its burstable CPU allocation model, the instance prioritizes budget efficiency over sustained throughput. Workloads requiring sustained high processor utilization will face CPU credit exhaustion and potential performance throttling. As a result, the t2.medium is best aligned with low-traffic web serving, lightweight staging and development servers, periodic background automation tasks, and small in-memory microservices.

The configuration allocates two vCPUs across two physical cores alongside 4.0 GB of memory, equating to 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware provisioning excludes dedicated GPUs and local instance storage, relying entirely on remote block storage with a baseline network rate of 0 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks reflect its entry-level profile, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 1519.0, a PassMark CPU mark of 2834.28, and Redis write operations reaching 1.09 million operations per second. The t2.medium is primarily suited for dev-test sandboxes, internal tools, microservices, and modest web servers.
